review.seat: Sol — structure, sequencing, engineering completeness and real FE front-kit readiness
review.one_line_summary: Proceed with W0 truth repair and a constrained W1 spine, but make the analytical kit screens traceable to explicit assumptions and bring a lightweight Blender envelope/assembly pass forward only after capacitor and inverter envelopes are bounded; `duty_screen=false`, `ship_ok=false`, and Bar B remains wholly open.
review.highest_overclaim_risk: A polished verdict page, capacitor screen and Blender assembly being read as a validated, package-feasible FE front kit when Path B is only a SIGHT-candidate, `torque_reliable=false`, duty capability is unproven, interfaces are absent, and all Bar B evidence remains open.

blender_earlier_than_w2.why: Move only W3.1 plus a deliberately non-release W3.2-lite forward in parallel with W2.1/W2.2: establish an envelope-controlled assembly hierarchy, interface placeholders and labelled unknown volumes. Do not create final hero renders, detailed cooling/HV routing, or claim packaging closure before the capacitor volume, inverter class, DC-link/busbar topology and cold-plate land assumptions are published. This improves Jack comprehension without letting aesthetics outrun engineering.

capacitors_first_kit_wedge.why: Yes. The DC-link is the most consequential missing power-electronics artefact because it connects DC voltage, current, PWM assumption, ripple-current capability, ESR/ESL, laminated-busbar loop inductance, cooling, volume, mass and inverter packaging. It creates useful constraints without pretending to select a supplier or close Bar B. Its output must be a bounded design-space screen with sensitivity cases, not a single pseudo-design point.

missing_workstreams: Requirements and operating-point control: establish a versioned requirements basis covering DC-link voltage range, current limits, PWM/switching-frequency range, ambient/coolant boundaries, duty-cycle definition, front-axle torque/speed request, regen limits and failure states. Every W2 calculation needs a source, status and validity range.

Interface-control-document workstream: publish provisional ICDs for HV, LV, coolant, mechanical mounts, shaft/spline or reducer output, sensors/CAN, service access, isolation clearances and bay-envelope datums. Mark unavailable partner dimensions as OPEN rather than substituting geometry.

Protection and functional-safety concept: HVIL, pre-charge/discharge, contactor ownership, insulation monitoring boundary, DC-link discharge time, over-current/over-voltage/over-temperature handling, fault containment and degraded-mode assumptions. A control-PCB honesty sheet alone is insufficient for a real front kit.

Electrical insulation and creepage/clearance screen: state voltage class, pollution/environment assumptions, connector and busbar separation targets, dielectric/hipot evidence needed, and all unknowns. This is necessary before visuals imply credible HV packaging.

Power-electronics loss and thermal budget integration: tie inverter switching/conduction losses, capacitor ESR loss, busbar loss and motor/gear losses to one transient heat-rejection budget. W2.2 should not be a disconnected ‘loss seed’.

Mass-properties and centre-of-gravity budget: allocate the stated 32 kg explicitly across motor, reducer, inverter, capacitor bank, cold plate, housings, connectors and fasteners, with reserve and uncertainty. A box volume alone does not establish kit feasibility.

Manufacturability, assembly and serviceability screen: casing split, sealing strategy, access to HV and coolant connections, capacitor retention, lifting/handling, tolerance stack, fastener strategy, potting/conformal-coating status and assembly sequence.

Rotordynamics and bearing-life boundary definition: the ripple-load sheet is useful, but bearing reactions need radial/axial loads, gear mesh loads, preload, lubrication, duty spectrum and speed range. Keep life prediction OPEN until these are available.

Driveline architecture closure: W2.12 is too late and too conditional. Gear ratio, torque/speed transformation, wheel-side load case, reduction-stage assumption, gear mesh force and lubrication concept are fundamental system constraints, not optional writeback.

Verification and validation plan: map each requirement and each Bar B item to analysis, bench test, dyno test, vehicle/lap evidence, acceptance criterion, owner, input required and closure authority. Partner asks should be generated from this matrix.

Configuration and provenance control: record the exact Path B input deck, solver/version, mesh/model status, assumptions, artefact hashes, restamp policy and consumer list. W0.4 coherence cannot prove technical validity; it only proves document consistency.

Regulatory and competition-rule basis: do not raise homologation, but record which Formula E/series rules, HV safety requirements and team/partner specifications are applicable, unknown or out of scope. ‘Homologation 1/10’ needs an evidence-plan basis, not merely a warning label.
phase_a_edits: Insert a Phase A gate immediately after W0.4: no W1/W2 artefact may be released until every numerical consumer of FE mean torque, required torque, Path B identity, dual-bar values, `torque_reliable`, `duty_screen` and `ship_ok` passes a machine-readable consistency check. Include figures, PNG captions, PDFs, workbook summaries and MANIFEST entries, not only the register.

Change W1.1 from a static verdict image to a versioned one-page evidence card with: artefact revision/hash; evaluated operating point; Path B mean 122.1 Nm at 24k/130; dual bars 104.1 Nm arch and 125.2 Nm bind; `torque_reliable=false`; `duty_screen=false`; `ship_ok=false`; model-validity statement; and an explicit statement that this is not a duty-capability or release claim.

Make W1.2 a closure-oriented open register rather than only a list: for B1–B10 and DEC-001…007 include evidence required, current status, owner, external dependency, acceptance criterion, and whether software can reduce risk but cannot close the item.

Expand W1.4 to include energy and control boundaries: HV source/contactors and pre-charge ownership, DC-link, inverter, motor, reducer/output, cold plate and coolant circuit, LV/CAN/control, sensors, safety/interlock boundary and all interfaces marked assumed/open/partner-owned.

Move W3.1 and a new W3.2-lite into Phase A, limited to an envelope box, named assemblies and conspicuous ‘concept volume / interface TBD’ tagging. Retain W3.3 hero, exploded and catalogue re-renders in Phase B after W2.1 and W2.2 review.

Rewrite W2.1 completion criteria to require an assumption table and sensitivity sweep over DC voltage, design current, PWM frequency, ripple model, allowable voltage ripple, capacitor temperature and derating. Report C_min, RMS ripple, ESR loss, ESL target, volume and mass as ranges; cite equations and input provenance; state that no lifetime, supplier part, mounting or qualification claim is made.

Combine W2.1 and W2.3 into a single DC-link-and-commutation-loop screen or require a shared topology diagram. Capacitor sizing without explicit commutation-loop inductance, switching-current path and module placement can produce an internally inconsistent kit story.

Make W2.2 include an allocated mass/volume/heat budget and a reconciliation against the 32 kg kit figure, bay envelope 343×259×267, cold-plate land and service clearances. If the budget cannot close, publish the shortfall as an OPEN rather than preserving the 32 kg assertion unexamined.

Add a Phase A ‘requirements and assumptions ledger’ task before W2.1, with IDs for each assumption and a link from every calculation/chart to those IDs. Distinguish partner-provided inputs, engineering targets, arbitrary placeholders and model outputs.

Move W2.12 into Phase A as a decision-framing task, not a full mesh check: document the presently assumed ratio, its provenance, resulting output speed/torque implication at 24k, and the missing wheel/vehicle requirements. The full ratio and mesh validation remains Phase B/partner-gated.

Add W2.14 in Phase A: provisional HV safety and protection boundary sheet covering pre-charge, discharge, contactor/HVIL/IMD ownership, fault paths and the statement ‘architecture unresolved’. This is more fundamental to a front-kit concept than the rotor FoS graphic.

Require W2.5 thermal storyboard to separate modelled/intermittent results from continuous-duty inference, show inputs and boundary conditions, and state that 159 versus 99 is not a validated operational temperature limit absent thermal hardware and test evidence.

Change success metric ‘Kit completeness 5.5/10’ to ‘analytical-definition completeness’ and separately report ‘hardware/partner closure remains 1–2/10’. Avoid a single rising kit score that Jack could interpret as physical readiness.

Bring W5 partner asks forward as draft requests during Phase A, immediately after each relevant screen. W2.1 should create B4/B6 ask fields; W2.6 creates B6; W2.12 creates drivetrain/vehicle requirement asks. Do not wait for a finished software pack to discover missing inputs.

blocking_findings.issue: The plan correctly updates stale 81.56 Nm references, but W0 coherence is described as a document freshness check rather than a complete claim-control gate. Conflicting torque, duty, status or caption claims can survive in images, spreadsheets, exported PDFs and Blender annotations.
blocking_findings.fix: Create a canonical machine-readable claim ledger and require every released artefact to consume it or declare an exception. Search/render-check all numerical and status consumers before release; fail the gate on any stale Path B, dual-bar, `torque_reliable`, `duty_screen` or `ship_ok` value.

blocking_findings.issue: W2.1 risks becoming false precision because DC-link capacitance, RMS ripple, ESL and volume cannot be responsibly represented by one result without defined DC voltage range, modulation/PWM strategy, phase current waveform, switching frequency, allowable ripple, temperature, derating and topology.
blocking_findings.fix: Publish W2.1 as a bounded parametric design-space calculation with input provenance, equations, sensitivity ranges and an explicit topology. Label all outputs ‘screening targets’; prohibit lifetime, part-number, qualification and package-closure claims.

blocking_findings.issue: The plan lacks a controlled requirements and interface baseline. The bay envelope alone cannot support credible mass, cooling, connector, protection, mount, output-shaft or serviceability assertions.
blocking_findings.fix: Add a requirements-and-ICD workstream before or alongside W2. Define knowns, assumptions, owners, datum status and acceptance evidence for mechanical, HV, LV/CAN, coolant, shaft/driveline and service interfaces.

blocking_findings.issue: `duty_screen=false` is treated as a banner, but there is no explicit rule preventing W2 thermal, loss and capacitor screens from being reinterpreted as continuous-duty validation.
blocking_findings.fix: Add a claim taxonomy to every analysis: ‘screening’, ‘sign-consistent candidate’, ‘validated by test’, and ‘release’. Forbid continuous-duty, lap-duty, endurance, efficiency and thermal-capability claims unless their required evidence rows are closed.

blocking_findings.issue: Gear-ratio writeback is placed after several packaging tasks despite being a first-order determinant of output speed, output torque, gear forces, bearing loads, lubrication and vehicle relevance.
blocking_findings.fix: Advance a minimal ratio/provenance/output-implication note to Phase A. Keep detailed gear mesh, oil and life calculations open until vehicle and partner inputs are available.

blocking_findings.issue: The 32 kg figure and 343×259×267 envelope are used as design constraints but no allocation, reserve, centre-of-gravity or feasibility reconciliation is planned.
blocking_findings.fix: Add a mass-volume-CG ledger with component allocations, uncertainty and reserve. If the capacitor/inverter/cold-plate estimates exceed budget, flag a feasibility conflict rather than resizing Blender geometry to fit.

blocking_findings.issue: A real front HV kit needs an architecture-level safety boundary, while the plan only calls for a gate-drive/control PCB honesty sheet.
blocking_findings.fix: Add a provisional protection and HV safety sheet covering pre-charge/discharge, contactors, HVIL, IMD boundary, fusing, isolation, fault response and ownership. Keep each unprovided partner decision OPEN.

blocking_findings.issue: W3’s final renders can create packaging and manufacturability implications before topology, interfaces and cooling routing are sufficiently bounded.
blocking_findings.fix: Use a two-stage visual policy: Phase A concept-volume render with uncertainty labels; Phase B assembly render only after reviewed W2.1/W2.2/DC-loop outputs and a mass-volume reconciliation. Embed the same status legend in every hero image.

blocking_findings.issue: The partner-gated tasks are asks but not a verification plan with acceptance criteria, owners and closure authority; this makes Bar B likely to remain an unprioritised list.
blocking_findings.fix: Convert W5 into a verification and evidence matrix. For B1–B10 define test/request, fixture or data format, operating points, pass criterion, responsible partner, due date, evidence artefact and the authority permitted to close it.

blocking_findings.issue: The plan’s score targets could be read as advancement towards a buildable or homologation-ready kit despite the absence of hardware evidence.
blocking_findings.fix: Rename score outputs to ‘documentation/screening completeness’ and report a separate immutable partner-evidence status. Keep homologation at 1/10 and `ship_ok=false` in all phase summaries until qualified external evidence is returned.

review.one_line_summary: Doctrine is sound and honesty gates are right, but Phase A drops W0.4, over-scores kit lift while Bar B stays open, and dual-bar arithmetic must show Path B clears arch yet misses bind.
review.highest_overclaim_risk: Phase B kit completeness 6.5–7/10 and FE visual 7+/10 from analytical screens plus Blender while duty_screen=false, ship_ok=false and Bar B B1–B10 all open — reads as readiness inflation, not screen maturity.
review.blender_earlier_than_w2_why: W3.1 brief may run in parallel, but kit hierarchy and hero renders should follow W2.1–W2.2 volume/mass envelopes; early Blender without PE boxes recreates the generic industrial look and invites pretty-picture overclaim before Jack spine and OPEN register exist.
review.capacitors_first_kit_wedge_why: Largest Jack-visible PE hole closable from bus ripple/RMS/ESL physics without chassis XYZ, Gerbers or MPNs; correct first wedge ahead of inverter class tighten and any modal/NVH work.
missing_workstreams: Explicit dual-bar gap arithmetic on verdict (122.1 vs arch 104.1 vs bind 125.2, margin and shortfall)
W0.4 coherence enforce in Phase A commit series (listed in W0, omitted from §8)

EMC/EMI and HV creepage/clearance OPEN rows (not only PE packaging)
Dyno correlation plan linking Path B operating point to B1/B2 torque_reliable gate
Mass/budget roll-up single source (32 kg share vs bay 343×259×267) before Blender box freeze
Controls/torque-command path honesty (what is modelled vs NOT_FAB)

review.one_line_summary: Plan respects the W0→W1→W2→W3→W4→W5 doctrine, refuses to mint ship_ok, and correctly holds homologation at 1/10; lift claims are supportable, but Phase A needs caption-level tightening on thermal storyboard, capacitor envelope, inverter mass share, and Path B = dual bars framing.
review.highest_overclaim_risk: W2.1 DC-link capacitor concept screen — a 'screen' producing C_min, RMS ripple and a volume envelope is the single most overclaim-prone output in Phase A because (a) it is described as the 'first real kit-completeness lift', (b) the W3.2 Blender kit hierarchy explicitly depends on it for cap box sizing, and (c) Jack will read any drawn volume as a part, not a screen. Mitigation row mentions 'no MPN' but is silent on 'no committed volume / no binding envelope'.

blender_earlier_than_w2.why: W3.1 visual brief is launched in parallel with W2.1 (during W2, not before), and W3.2/W3.3 are correctly gated behind W2.1–W2.2 outputs for cap/inverter box sizing. The critical path keeps W0→W1→W2 ahead of W3.

capacitors_first_kit_wedge.why: W2.1 needs only bus voltage, design current and PWM class — no chassis XYZ, no Gerbers, no mount points. It is the largest visible gap in the 4/10 kit score and is the dependency that unblocks the Blender kit hierarchy (W3.2). Correctly sequenced before W2.2/W2.3.

missing_workstreams: No explicit captioning rule for the 'Path B = dual bars' coupling — 122.1 Nm is the dual-bar mean and dual-bar spread is 104.1/125.2; plan phrases this loosely as 'Path B + dual bars' which can read as two separate attributes.
No operating-point definition for '24k/130' in the artefact lineage (rpm is clear; 130 unit / meaning is not). Required before W0.1 restamp so restated numbers are auditable.
No provenance / corner-definition note for the iron-loss '3.9–8.5 kW class' band in W2.7 — speed/torque corners and solver basis not stated.
No 'no continuous 250 kW thermal clearance' caption doctrine for W2.5 — the 159/99 °C numbers will be read as magnet insulation clearance unless explicitly disclaimed.
No reverse-rationalisation test (per lift, ask: 'if duty_screen were true, would this lift still be valid?') — useful gate against cosmetic uplifts dressed as engineering.
No driving-cycle / race-stint anchor underpinning the 250 kW claim used in the scorecard — duty_screen false means the operating envelope is asserted, not measured.
No double-pulse ICD sketch referenced even though W2.3 flags it as Bar B — partner ask sheet would benefit from a one-line test definition now.
No 'screen envelope ≠ committed volume' rule stated anywhere as a hard ban — only in the risk table as a soft mitigation.

review.one_line_summary: Proceed, but only after W0 truth gates and explicit non-sign-off captions; keep Blender and homologation behind W0/W1/W2, and treat capacitors as an analytical wedge rather than a closed BOM.

blender_earlier_than_w2.why: Only W3.1 reference brief may run in parallel; W3.2 and W3.3 must wait for W2.1/W2.2 stamped visual-only envelopes, otherwise Blender freezes false packaging and creates Jack optics ahead of engineering depth.

capacitors_first_kit_wedge.why: DC-link capacitors are the most visible kit-completeness gap and can be screened from bus voltage, ripple, PWM class, ESL, temperature and volume without chassis XYZ or invented MPNs; they also define a clean Bar B ask and a realistic FE/China supply-chain class discussion.

EMC/EMI proximity screen for busbar, capacitor, gate-drive and sensor harness routing, without inventing layout or supplier parts.

Visual-versus-engineering geometry control, so Blender envelopes are tagged non-authoritative until real interfaces exist.
FE/China supply-chain realism screen for capacitor and inverter classes, covering voltage/current/temperature class, lead-time and qualification route, with no invented MPNs or supplier claims.
Test-to-model correlation plan for dyno, flow bench, gear-oil and lap-log data before W5 asks are sent.
Pack rebuild acceptance checklist with manifest hash, stale-number grep and scorecard gates.
